question: Should OpenClaw define a core skill permission manifest now, and if so should the first phase be inspect-only metadata, enforced install/update consent, or signing-backed runtime policy?
rationale: The issue crosses security boundaries, skill package format, ClawHub trust metadata, install UX, runtime enforcement, and upgrade compatibility; automation cannot choose the permanent contract safely.

options.title: Adopt staged core contract
options.body: Define a versioned inspectable manifest first, then add consent and enforcement semantics once the compatibility story is explicit.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub/plugin policy
options.body: Keep core unchanged and let external tools or ClawHub metadata provide advisory permission reporting until an enforcement API is needed.

options.title: Split into narrower RFCs
options.body: Track manifest schema, audit UI, signing, attestation, and enforcement as separate owner-reviewed issues before implementation.

recommendation.title: Adopt staged core contract
recommendation.body: Define a versioned inspectable manifest first, then add consent and enforcement semantics once the compatibility story is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across skills CLI, ClawHub install policy, and security hardening decisions relevant to this contract.
